text: Most hydraulic failures start with dirt you can't see.
A moulding machine's clamp, injection and ejectors are all driven by oil under pressure.
Oil returning to the tank passes through a filter.
Inside is a pleated element: a huge area of fine media, folded small.
Oil flows from the outside in, and particles are trapped on the media.
On top sits a bypass valve, held shut by a spring,
and an indicator shows the pressure drop across the element.
As the element loads with dirt, that pressure drop climbs.
At the bypass setting, the valve opens,
and dirty oil flows straight past the element.
Those particles wear the pump and jam the valves.
Warning signs: the indicator in the red, a noisy pump, and rising particle counts in oil samples.
So: change the element when the indicator says so, not just by the calendar.
Never keep running in the red.
Use the right element, and check the seals.
And sample the oil to confirm it's clean.
